corrections.text: The article lists what the docs' data-and-access page says the server sends to Anthropic (up to three ID headers, a credential check every 60 seconds, a User-Agent header that Anthropic can use to count usage) and says it cannot tell whether these are the 'Usage Signals' of section 5.9. The same page also describes a label, 'cma-server', carried in the request body as metadata.user_id on calls to the Claude API, to Microsoft Foundry and to a gateway that accepts the same requests as the Claude API, which Anthropic 'can use ... to count usage of self-hosted Managed Agents' even if a proxy removed the User-Agent header. The article does not mention it.

The article contrasts The New Stack's 'unless Anthropic expressly permits them' with section 3(c)'s 'as the Documentation expressly permits', saying the license 'names the documentation rather than Anthropic'. Section 1.6 of the license defines 'Documentation' as 'the integration guides, release notes, and other technical documentation that Anthropic delivers with the Licensed Code'; the article does not give that definition, and the license does not say whether Anthropic's public docs pages are that Documentation.

The article says 'Anthropic's total liability is capped at US$100,000.00 (8.2)'. Section 8.2 opens 'To the maximum extent permitted by law' and also excludes liability for indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages and for loss of profits, revenue or data; the article gives the amount without those qualifiers.
